newsitem.title: UK: Cookson sees return to earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Cookson sees return to earnings growth.

text.p: British electronic, ceramic and plastic industrial materials company Cookson Group Plc said on Thursday it expected to resume earnings growth in the latter half of this year after profits turned lower in 1996.

"We expect trading conditions to remain unchanged for the balance of the first half. A return to growth in earnings is then anticipated, the extent of which is dependent upon both the recovery in the electronics industry and the course of sterling," chief executive Richard Oster said.
Earlier on Thursday, Cookson said pretax profit before exceptional items dropped by eight percent last year to 166 million, while group turnover rose four percent to 1.88 billion pounds ($3 billion).
Despite the drop in earnings, Cookson raised its final dividend to 4.7 pence per share from 4.5 pence a year earlier, bringing the total dividend to 8.6 pence, up from eight pence.
In the year to date, Oster said the company's Advanced Refractories, Engineering Products and Plastics divisions continued to maintain a satisfactory performance.

But he said Cookson Matthey Ceramics, the joint venture with Johnson Matthey still faced difficult conditions in the zircon business, while business at the electronics division, where sales in organic terms dropped two percent last year, remained little changed.
